comparable_reason: The task's outputs split cleanly and I measured both halves. The HT-SR exponent IS comparable: `avg_alpha_official` has Spearman +0.180 with d_model (p = 0.21) and +0.169 with n_layers (p = 0.24) over 51 archived models whose configs resolve, and -0.082 / +0.167 (p = 0.82 / 0.65) over a fresh 10-model local panel -- it is dimensionless by construction. `avg_stable_rank` is NOT: rho = +0.8885 with d_model (p = 3.36e-18, n = 51) and +0.8899 with log-parameters (p = 8.84e-22, n = 61) in the archive, +0.734 (p = 0.016) and +0.766 with n_layers (p = 0.0098) on the fresh panel, and it is structurally bounded above by min(m, n). `avg_alpha_hat = alpha * log10(lambda_max)` multiplies the dimensionless exponent by a scale-dependent norm and reads rho = -0.841 with vocab_size (p = 0.0023, n = 10). paper_reason: Martin, Peng & Mahoney (Nat Commun 12:4122, arXiv 2002.06716) Table 2 gives GPT2-small: 49 layers treated, weighted alpha (alpha_hat) = 9.62. confounds_reason: For `avg_stable_rank` the confound is confirmed and its mechanism is structural: stable rank = ||W||_F^2/||W||_2^2 is bounded above by min(m, n), and it measures rho = +0.8885 with d_model (p = 3.36e-18, n = 51 archived models) and +0.8899 with log-parameters (p = 8.84e-22, n = 61); on a fresh 10-model panel it is +0.734 (p = 0.016). The archive does show `avg_alpha_official` rho = +0.738 with vocab_size (p = 6.45e-10, n = 51), but my fresh 10-model panel gives exactly 0.000 for the same pair, so the archived vocabulary association is a model-FAMILY effect (vocab is essentially a family label in that zoo), not a mechanical one.
